facts.statement: Marmornectes is an extinct genus of pliosaurid from the Middle Jurassic of Bedfordshire, United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Marmornectes is a genus of pliosaurid known from the Middle Jurassic of Bedfordshire, United Kingdom.

facts.statement: The genus Marmornectes and its type species Marmornectes candrewi were named by Hilary F. Ketchum and Roger B. J. Benson in 2011.
facts.quote: Marmornectes was first named by Hilary F. Ketchum and Roger B. J. Benson in 2011 and the type species is Marmornectes candrewi.

facts.statement: The generic name Marmornectes means "marble-swimmer", combining Latin and Greek roots.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from marmor, Latin for "marble", and nectes, Greek for "swimmer", thus the meaning is "marble-swimmer".

facts.statement: The specific name candrewi honors Chris Andrew, who found the only known specimen and donated it to the Bedford Museum in 1998.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Chris Andrew for finding the only known specimen and donating it to Bedford Museum in 1998.

facts.statement: Marmornectes lived during the early Callovian stage of the late Middle Jurassic, approximately 164.7 to 163.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was collected in 1999 from the Sigaloceras enodatum ammonoid subzone of the Peterborough Member, Oxford Clay Formation, which dates to the early Callovian stage of the late Middle Jurassic, about 164.7-163.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: Marmornectes was a longirostrine pliosaurid characterized by seven unique features and is most similar to Peloneustes philarchus.
facts.quote: It was a longirostrine pliosaurid with seven autapomorphies, and is most similar to Peloneustes philarchus.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis indicates that Marmornectes is basal to Peloneustes and other pliosaurids.
facts.quote: Nevertheless, a cladistic analysis found it to be basal to Peloneustes and other pliosaurids.

facts.statement: Marmornectes is an extinct genus of pliosaurid that lived during the Middle Jurassic in what is now Great Britain.
facts.quote: Marmornectes es un género extinto de pliosáurido que vivió durante el Jurásico Medio en lo que ahora es Gran Bretaña.

facts.statement: The time range for Marmornectes is the Callovian stage, from 165.3 to 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The known fossil material of Marmornectes consists of the holotype BEDFM 1999.201, an articulated partial skeleton that includes the skull.
rejected.quote: Marmornectes is known from the holotype BEDFM 1999.201, an articulated partial skeleton which includes the skull.
